items.title: What Does AT&T Stock Do To Your Money When The Market Falls?
items.summary: AT&T (T) is up 4.4% over the last five trading days, while the S&P 500 is down 1.1%. Strength in a weak tape pulls money in. That five-day move is not the question. The question is what holding AT&T does to your money when the market moves, because over the past year it has tended to go the other way.

items.title: Verizon and AT&T Dominate Communications Services. Why That’s a Problem.
items.summary: The recent outperformance of  Verizon  and  AT&T  is not the kind of leadership that typically accompanies a durable growth cycle.  Both names posted mid-to high-single-digit gains over the past month, while many of the growthier, internet, and entertainment stocks that dominate the  (XLC) have lagged or declined.  Verizon is up 26% year to date, comfortably outperforming flashier sector peers like  Alphabet  up 10%,  Meta Platforms  up 2%, and  Netflix  down 17%.

items.title: How a Roth IRA Can Keep Thousands More of Your High-Yield Dividend Income Compounding
items.summary: Where you hold a high-yield dividend stock matters almost as much as which one you pick, and for ordinary-income payers like BDCs and REITs, the wrong account quietly erodes a portion of every distribution before it ever compounds.

items.title: Is Comcast Stock Cheap Or Just Shrinking?
items.summary: Comcast (CMCSA) generated free cash over the past twelve months worth 20.1% of its market value. The median S&P 500 company manages 4.4%. Part of that gap is Comcast's debt. The rest means one of two things: the market has made a mistake, or the cash is about to get smaller. Comcast keeps losing broadband customers, and that is the market's answer.
